title: Dedicated gateway callback deduplication merges near-simultaneous JSON responses causing structured-output parser corruption
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A production customer (enterprise, Dedicated) reported that function/tool call responses occasionally arrive to their service with fields merged across two distinct callback payloads. The platform-level structured-output parser then fails to extract valid JSON objects, producing corrupted outputs and downstream application errors. Scope: affects Dedicated gateway and Private deployments using the internal callback multiplexing layer; Hosted customers appear less frequently affected because their connection topology avoids the dedup code path. Impact: multiple customer incidents over the last 48 hours, several production requests returned malformed structured outputs causing retries and user-facing failures. Reproducibility: race condition under high concurrency when two callbacks for different invocations arrive within ~3-10ms on the same gateway worker and an internal deduplication routine incorrectly collapses them into a single envelope.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure Dedicated Gateway with callback multiplexing enabled and reduced worker buffer timeout (test harness mode).
2) Send two function call responses from downstream toolserver with distinct invocation IDs but identical callback correlation IDs within <10ms of each other (test script provided).
3) Observe gateway logs merge the two JSON bodies into a single envelope separated by no delimiter, which the structured-output parser then mis-parses as a combined object.
4) Unit test reproducer attached (scripts/repro/callback_race.py) used by SRE/eng to validate fix.
observed_behavior: When the race occurs, gateway dedup logic matches on correlation id only and removes what it believes is a duplicate while concatenating payload buffers. Result: JSON objects are concatenated without a safe boundary and downstream parser errors with 'unexpected token' or silently returns the first object and drops fields from second object.
root_cause_analysis: 1) Deduplication key omitted per-connection sequence header; only correlation id was used. 2) Short-lived buffer coalescing for throughput merged adjacent buffers without adding framing in the shared path. 3) Under high throughput and CPU scheduling jitter (seen on Dedicated), two callbacks sharing correlation id and arriving in micro-burst hit the same worker and were collapsed. 4) Private deployments that had custom proxy timeouts amplified the window where coalescing would occur.
mitigation_and_workarounds: 1) Temporary: Customers can disable callback multiplexing via gateway config toggle 'callback_multiplexing=false' (affects throughput; documented workaround shared with customer).
2) Temporary: Increase connection-level callback delimiter enforcement by setting 'callback_buffer_timeout_ms' to 0 to force immediate flush (may increase p99 latency).
3) SRE rolled out conservative rate-limiting rules for affected tenants to reduce collision frequency while fix is deployed.
4) We notified affected customers and provided a scoped PR they could apply for self-hosted private instances.
fix_summary: Implemented a three-part fix: (a) expand deduplication key to include tenant_id + invocation_sequence_header + correlation_id, (b) stop coalescing adjacent callback buffers without explicit framing — add a lightweight delimiter header and enforce single-envelope flush semantics, and (c) add a defensive parser fallback that rejects concatenated payloads instead of silently merging. Backwards compatibility: gateway negotiates framing; legacy callers unaffected (old behavior preserved until gateway sets framing=required after rollout window).
implementation_details: Added unit tests: callback_mux_test.go reproducer + fuzz test for parser against concatenated envelopes
Added integration test: dedicated/integration/callback_race_integration.sh runs stress harness and asserts no merged payloads for 60s at 2000 RPS per worker.
deployment_plan: 1) Canary runtime-1.20.1-hotfix to 5% Dedicated pool in staging — validate with customer repro harness (24h).
2) If green, increase to 30% and monitor parsing error rate and invocation latencies (6h).
3) Full roll to Dedicated clusters over 12 hours with per-tenant throttles; Private customers receive patch bundle and instructions.
4) Hosted: deploy to API edge after Dedicated rollout verification (to minimize risk).
5) Post-deploy: run end-to-end verification using customer-supplied test traces and our stress harness.
Rollback: revert to previous runtime if parsing error rate increases; fallback: disable multiplexing via config for affected tenants.
test_plan: - Unit: assert dedup key includes sequence header and tenant id; negative tests for near-simultaneous arrivals.
- Integration: stress harness for 2M callbacks/hour verifying no merged payloads.
- E2E: customer-provided trace replay validation (we have consented traces from 3 customers).
- Chaos: CPU scheduling jitter test on Dedicated worker to reproduce race and validate fix.
metrics_and_alerts: - New metric: gateway.callback_merge_attempts (counter) - alert on >0 after rollout for 1h
- Parse error rate alert tightened for runtime-1.20.* (pager if >0.1% over 5m for affected tenants),
- Latency SLO monitor for callback round-trip to ensure framing doesn't regress p99 by >10%.
Dashboards: shared link to staging run and customer replay dashboards (Grafana link in links).
